transcript.text: Thank you all for those critical updates. Let me summarize what I'm hearing and the tensions we need to resolve before I can approve. Jonas, you're telling us the green-bond framework requires a green label, annual allocation reporting, and external review — and the eligible project pool is exactly $18 million, matching our issuance size. Maya, your anchor investor requires a 4-year maturity and a coupon no higher than 5.25%, which conflicts with the preliminary 3-year, 5.50% terms. Victor, your treasury model shows $10 million must go to refinancing a 2027 maturity, which is relevant to the maturity question. And Leah, legal requires a make-whole redemption clause and a 12-month no-redemption period. So the key issues are: (1) maturity — 3 years vs. 4 years, with the 2027 refinancing need and the anchor investor both pulling toward a longer tenor; (2) coupon — 5.50% vs. the anchor's 5.25% cap; and (3) incorporating the green framework requirements and redemption protections into the final term sheet. I'd like each of you to give me your concise, final recommendation on how to reconcile these terms so I can make the approval decision in this review.

transcript.text: Here's my concise sustainability recommendation for reconciling the terms. First, on the green framework: the $18 million eligible project pool matches the issuance size exactly, so we can proceed with a green-labeled bond — but the final term sheet must explicitly include (a) a green label, (b) a commitment to annual allocation reporting, and (c) a requirement to obtain an external second-party review or SPO before launch. These are non-negotiable under our framework. Second, on maturity: a 4-year maturity is fully compatible with our green-bond framework — the framework does not constrain tenor, and a longer tenor may actually be preferable for environmental projects that have multi-year deployment timelines. I would support moving to 4 years to accommodate both the anchor investor and the 2027 refinancing need Victor flagged. Third, on coupon: the 5.25% cap is outside my sustainability remit, but from a green-bond perspective there is no conflict — green labels do not require a premium coupon. My bottom line: I can support approval of a 4-year, 5.25% green-labeled bond with annual allocation reporting, external review, and the redemption protections Leah described, provided all of those features are reflected in the final term sheet Elena signs off on.

However, the key point is that the 4-year tenor accommodates both the anchor investor's hard requirement and provides adequate proceeds to cover the 2027 maturity when it comes due. The remaining $8 million can fund the approved environmental projects Jonas confirmed. I support 4 years. Second, on coupon: reducing from 5.50% to 5.25% to meet the anchor investor's cap is acceptable from a treasury standpoint. The 25 basis point reduction is modest, and securing the anchor's committed allocation de-risks the syndication. The green-label features should help broaden demand to compensate for any pricing concession. Third, on the green framework and redemption protections: the green label, annual allocation reporting, and external review are compatible with our treasury requirements — the $18 million eligible project pool matches the issuance size, and the $10 million refinancing allocation can be clearly tracked in the annual allocation report. The make-whole redemption clause and 12-month no-redemption period Leah described are standard and do not conflict with our refinancing plan. One action item: I will attach the refinancing instruction to the term-sheet folder immediately after this review so the documentation reflects the $10 million allocation to the 2027 maturity. My bottom line: I can support approval of a 4-year, 5.25% green-labeled bond with annual allocation reporting, external review, and the redemption protections, provided all features are reflected in the final term sheet Elena signs off on.
